# Best RV power station and solar combos

The best pick depends on whether you need to run a roof AC. I couldn't open retailer pages, so I can't give exact current prices or direct product links. The links below go to the reviews with buy buttons, and you should confirm specs and price on the retailer's page.

## My picks

**1. Full-time RV or boondocking with AC: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It can expand past 12kWh and recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W while running, so one battery runs it for roughly 2.3 hours. That is why you'd add expansion batteries or run AC only part-time.
- It weighs a lot, and moving it is a two-person job.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**2. Best mid-range for solar: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W and a 1,200W solar input, the highest in the 2kWh class. It also has a built-in 30A RV outlet and weighs about 62 lb.
- Pair it with a large array, such as 400-800W of rooftop or folding panels. A small panel would waste its ceiling.
- Sources: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) and [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**3. Weekend trips with no AC: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 plus two SolarSaga 200W panels**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W and is about 23.8 lb. Two 200W panels use its full 400W solar input, and adding more won't speed up charging.
- This is enough for a 12V fridge, CPAP, laptops and Starlink Mini.
- Source: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Runner-up for AC: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- It has 3,024Wh, 3,000W and 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

## Buying tips
- **Match the panels to the solar input limit.** The Jackery 2000 v2 accepts only 400W, while the Bluetti AC200L takes 1,200W. Check this first.
- **Check the RV outlet.** If you want to feed the trailer's shore inlet, look for a 30A port (or use a TT-30 adapter, as with the DELTA Pro 3).
- **Size by watt-hours.** Multiply your load by hours. A 150W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh.
- **Stick with LiFePO4.** All the current models above use it, rated for 3,000+ cycles.
- **Spec conflicts between sources.** One source lists the 30A RV outlet on the older AC200P and another on the AC200L, so confirm on the product page.

One search result (a Dealectric page for the ALLPOWERS R4000) contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored that. The R4000 is a 45 kg, 3.5kWh unit, which is heavy for most RVers anyway.

If you tell me whether you need to run an AC, your fridge and device loads, and your budget, I can narrow this to one unit and a panel size.
